why.correct: Let <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = x^2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u^2 - 5u + 4</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (u - 1)(u - 4)</annotation></semantics></math>. So <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^4 - 5x^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 4</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (x^2 - 1)(x^2 - 4)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (x - 1)(x + 1)(x - 2)(x + 2)</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Correct as a first step, but each factor is a difference of squares and splits again.

Right: treat it as a quadratic in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2</annotation></semantics></math>, then split each difference of squares.

This has <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^3</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> terms when multiplied out; <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^4 - 5x^2 + 4</annotation></semantics></math> has none.

This multiplies to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^4 + 5x^2 + 4</annotation></semantics></math>: the sign of the middle term is wrong.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4x^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 4x</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 1 - (x^2 - 6x + 9)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 4x^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 4x</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 1 - x^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 6x - 9</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3x^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>10</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 10x - 8</annotation></semantics></math>.

Factor: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(x - 3)(x + 3) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>. A product is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> when a factor is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3</annotation></semantics></math>. Never divide by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>; it hides <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Dividing both sides by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> loses the solution <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Factor instead.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^3 = 9x</annotation></semantics></math> does not mean <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 9</annotation></semantics></math>; <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>9</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>81</mn><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9^3 - 81 \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

Right: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(x - 3)(x + 3) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, and each factor gives a solution.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 = 9</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">±</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \pm 3</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">±</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 9</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: Sum of cubes with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a = x</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = 4</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^3 + b^3</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2)</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^3 + 64</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>16</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (x + 4)(x^2 - 4x + 16)</annotation></semantics></math>. Multiplying back, the middle terms cancel.
options: In a sum of cubes the middle term of the second factor is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-ab</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-4x</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+4x</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x + 4)^3</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>48</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= x^3 + 12x^2 + 48x + 64</annotation></semantics></math>, which has two extra terms.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a = x</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is the difference of cubes, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^3 - 64</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + 16</annotation></semantics></math> is a sum of squares. It is at least <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> for every real <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, so it has no real zeros and no real factors.
options: Difference of squares: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x - 4)(x + 4)</annotation></semantics></math>.
A sum of squares has no real zeros, so it has no real factors.

A perfect square: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x + 4)^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

Common factor: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>16</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(x - 16)</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3x - 2)(3x - 2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 9x^2 - 6x - 6x</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 4</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 9x^2 - 12x</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

A polynomial is a sum of terms <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">ax^n</annotation></semantics></math> with whole-number exponents <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3}{x}</annotation></semantics></math> has the variable in a denominator, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + \frac{3}{x}</annotation></semantics></math> is not a polynomial.
options: Each term is a number times a whole-number power of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.

The order of the terms does not matter: this is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-x^5 + 6</annotation></semantics></math>.
A fraction as a coefficient is fine; the exponent <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> is a whole number.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3}{x}</annotation></semantics></math> divides by the variable, which a polynomial does not do.

why.correct: If <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x - 2</annotation></semantics></math> is a factor, then <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(2) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8 + 2k - 6 = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2k = -2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k = -1</annotation></semantics></math>. Check: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^3 - x - 6</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (x - 2)(x^2 + 2x + 3)</annotation></semantics></math>.

Dividing by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> assumes <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math> does solve the equation: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>0</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0^3 = 4(0)</annotation></semantics></math>. Factor instead: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^3 - 4x</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= x(x - 2)(x + 2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math>.

A square root has two signs: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-2)^2 = 4</annotation></semantics></math> too, so both are solutions.

A negative exponent means the reciprocal: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{-3} = \frac{1}{2^3} = \frac{1}{8}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3^{-2} = \frac{1}{9}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>27</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">27^{-2/3}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mroot><mn>27</mn><mn>3</mn></mroot><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{(\sqrt[3]{27})^2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{9}</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Reciprocal of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

The cube root of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>27</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">27</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>; squared, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9</annotation></semantics></math>; the negative exponent gives <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{9}</annotation></semantics></math>.

This is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-(3^2) = -9</annotation></semantics></math>.
This is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>9</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{9} = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: When you multiply powers of the same base, keep the base and add the exponents: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>7</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^3 \cdot 2^4 = 2^7 = 128</annotation></semantics></math>. The student's <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>7</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>384</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4^7 = 16{,}384</annotation></semantics></math> is far too large.
options: Multiplying exponents is for a power of a power, like <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2^3)^4</annotation></semantics></math>.
Keep the base, add the exponents.
Bases are never combined by this rule, and exponents are added, not multiplied.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>7</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^7 = 128</annotation></semantics></math> but <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>7</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>384</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4^7 = 16{,}384</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: Divide, same base, subtract exponents: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>4</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{5^6}{5^4} = 5^2 = 25</annotation></semantics></math>. Zero exponent: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7^0 = 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Sum: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>26</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">26</annotation></semantics></math>.

The root as a power: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mroot><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></mroot><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt[3]{x} = x^{1/3}</annotation></semantics></math>. Divide, same base, subtract exponents: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^2}{x^{1/3}}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= x^{2 - 1/3}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= x^{5/3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9 = 3^2</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>9</mn><mi>t</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>t</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9^t = (3^2)^t</annotation></semantics></math>. A power of a power multiplies the exponents: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3^{2t}</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>t</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3^2)^t = 3^{2 \cdot t}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3^{t + 2} = 9 \cdot 3^t</annotation></semantics></math>. Adding exponents comes from multiplying powers, not from a power of a power.

The exponents multiply, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 \cdot t</annotation></semantics></math>; <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> is not squared.

The <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> is an exponent on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>, not a factor in front. At <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>9</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>81</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9^2 = 81</annotation></semantics></math>, but <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>18</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 \cdot 3^2 = 18</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: Write both sides as powers of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{8} = \frac{1}{2^3} = 2^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math>. Equal powers of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> have equal exponents: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x + 1 = -3</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -4</annotation></semantics></math>. Check: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{-3} = \frac{1}{8}</annotation></semantics></math>.

Subtracting exponents comes from dividing powers of the same base: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5^{x - 2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{5^x}{5^2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mn>25</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{5^x}{25}</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: A difference in the exponent is a quotient of powers, not a difference of powers. At <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5^0 = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, but <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25 - 25 = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5^2 = 25</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5^{x - 2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 5^x \cdot 5^{-2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mn>25</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{5^x}{25}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25 \cdot 5^x = 5^{x + 2}</annotation></semantics></math>. The exponent <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math> divides by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: Inside first: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^4}{x} = x^{4 - 1} = x^3</annotation></semantics></math>. Power of a power: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x^3)^{-2} = x^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math>. Negative exponent: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{-6} = \frac{1}{x^6}</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: The exponent is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math>, so the result is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math>, the reciprocal of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^6</annotation></semantics></math>.
A negative exponent makes a reciprocal, not a negative number.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^4}{x} = x^3</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^4</annotation></semantics></math>: the <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> in the denominator has exponent <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x^3)^{-2} = x^{-6} = \frac{1}{x^6}</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: Negative exponent first: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\frac{4}{9}\right)^{-1/2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \left(\frac{9}{4}\right)^{1/2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Sine is opposite over hypotenuse. From <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> the opposite side is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>17</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin B = \frac{8}{17}</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Opposite <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> over hypotenuse <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>17</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>15</mn><mn>17</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{15}{17}</annotation></semantics></math> is adjacent over hypotenuse, which is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos B</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>15</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{8}{15}</annotation></semantics></math> is opposite over adjacent, which is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan B</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: From <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math>: opposite <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 15</annotation></semantics></math>, adjacent <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 8</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>15</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan C = \frac{15}{8}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The ladder is the hypotenuse. The height on the wall is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{10^2 - 6^2} = 8</annotation></semantics></math> feet, opposite <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>; the 6 feet is adjacent. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan\theta = \frac{8}{6} = \frac{4}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Opposite <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> over adjacent <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math>.
This is adjacent over opposite, the ratio upside down.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>6</mn><mn>10</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{6}{10}</annotation></semantics></math> is adjacent over hypotenuse, which is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>10</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{8}{10}</annotation></semantics></math> is opposite over hypotenuse, which is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>55</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>h</mi><mn>40</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin 55^\circ = \frac{h}{40}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.8192</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>32.768</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h = 40(0.8192) = 32.768</annotation></semantics></math> meters.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mtext>adjacent</mtext><mn>8</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\theta = \frac{\text{adjacent}}{8}</annotation></semantics></math>, so adjacent <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 8\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.

Draw a triangle with opposite <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> and hypotenuse <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math>. The adjacent side is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{25 - 9} = 4</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos A = \frac{4}{5}</annotation></semantics></math>. Any triangle with this angle gives the same ratio.
options: Adjacent <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> over hypotenuse <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math>.

This flips <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin A</annotation></semantics></math> upside down; cosine needs the adjacent side.

This is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 - \frac{3}{5}</annotation></semantics></math>. Sides follow the Pythagorean theorem, not subtraction of ratios.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3}{4}</annotation></semantics></math> is opposite over adjacent, which is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan A</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: Both sides in the ratio are multiplied by 3, so the ratio does not change. A trigonometric ratio depends only on the angle.
options: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mtext>opposite</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mtext>hypotenuse</mtext></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3 \cdot \text{opposite}}{3 \cdot \text{hypotenuse}}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mtext>opposite</mtext><mtext>hypotenuse</mtext></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The opposite side triples, but so does the hypotenuse, so the 3s cancel.
Areas scale by 9, but a ratio of two lengths does not change.
Nothing shrinks: the factor 3 appears on top and bottom and cancels.

why.correct: The rise is opposite <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> and the horizontal run is adjacent: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>24</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan\theta = \frac{2}{24} = \frac{1}{12}</annotation></semantics></math>, the slope of the ramp.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>50</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>h</mi><mn>30</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan 50^\circ = \frac{h}{30}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.192</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>35.76</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h = 30(1.192) = 35.76</annotation></semantics></math> meters.

Name the sides, pick the ratio that uses both, clear the fraction, then solve: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>0.6</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{9}{0.6} = 15</annotation></semantics></math>.

First the hypotenuse: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mn>9</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>12</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>225</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{9^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{225} = 15</annotation></semantics></math>. From <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math>, the adjacent side is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mn>15</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos A = \frac{12}{15} = \frac{4}{5}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The tower is opposite the angle and the distance <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> is adjacent: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>40</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>21</mn><mi>d</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan 40^\circ = \frac{21}{d}</annotation></semantics></math>. Multiply by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>40</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>21</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d \tan 40^\circ = 21</annotation></semantics></math>. Divide: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>21</mn><mn>0.84</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d = \frac{21}{0.84} = 25</annotation></semantics></math> meters.

The leg opposite <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> is the leg adjacent to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>: moving to the other acute angle swaps the names of the legs. So <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos B</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mtext>adjacent to </mtext><mi>B</mi></mrow><mtext>hypotenuse</mtext></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\text{adjacent to } B}{\text{hypotenuse}}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mtext>opposite </mtext><mi>A</mi></mrow><mtext>hypotenuse</mtext></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\text{opposite } A}{\text{hypotenuse}}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \sin A</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>13</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{5}{13}</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mn>13</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{12}{13}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos A</annotation></semantics></math> (and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin B</annotation></semantics></math>): it uses the other leg, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12</annotation></semantics></math>.

The side opposite <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> is adjacent to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>, so the two ratios are the same.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{5}{12}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan A</annotation></semantics></math>, a ratio of the two legs.

A cosine of an acute angle is less than <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>, because the hypotenuse is the longest side.

why.correct: Choose the ratio that uses the side you know and the side you want. Adjacent and hypotenuse are the two sides in cosine: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>25</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos 25^\circ</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mtext>adjacent</mtext><mtext>hypotenuse</mtext></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Sine uses the opposite side and the hypotenuse; the known side is adjacent.
Tangent uses the two legs and leaves out the hypotenuse.
CAH: cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse.

One side and one acute angle are enough: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mtext>hypotenuse</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{hypotenuse}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mtext>adjacent</mtext><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>25</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\text{adjacent}}{\cos 25^\circ}</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: Opposite and adjacent are the two sides in tangent: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mtext>opposite</mtext><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan\theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{5}</annotation></semantics></math>, so opposite <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 5\tan\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mtext>opposite</mtext><mtext>hypotenuse</mtext></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the hypotenuse is the longest side, so the ratio is between <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.2</annotation></semantics></math> would need a leg longer than the hypotenuse. (For <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.2</annotation></semantics></math> would be fine.)
options: A very small angle has a very short opposite side, so a sine near <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> is possible.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>30</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin 30^\circ = 0.5</annotation></semantics></math>.

An angle close to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>90</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90^\circ</annotation></semantics></math> has a sine close to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>.
A sine above <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> would make the opposite leg longer than the hypotenuse.

why.correct: The sides are in the ratio <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 : 1 : \sqrt{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, so the hypotenuse is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6\sqrt{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

Scale <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>:</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 : \sqrt{3} : 2</annotation></semantics></math> by 5 so that the hypotenuse is 10: the legs are <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math> is across from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>60</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>.

In the 30-60-90 triangle the side across from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>60</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60^\circ</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math> and the hypotenuse is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>60</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Opposite <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math> over hypotenuse <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>30</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin 30^\circ</annotation></semantics></math> (or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>60</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos 60^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>): it uses the short leg.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math> is opposite over adjacent, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>60</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan 60^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> belongs to the 45-45-90 triangle.

why.correct: In the 45-45-90 triangle with legs 1, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>45</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos 45^\circ</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>80</mn><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{80}{360} \cdot 2\pi(9)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mn>18</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{2}{9} \cdot 18\pi</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 4\pi</annotation></semantics></math> cm.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>θ</mi><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\theta}{360} \cdot 2\pi r = r</annotation></semantics></math>. Divide by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>θ</mi><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\theta}{360} \cdot 2\pi = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>360</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{360}{2\pi}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>180</mn><mi>π</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{180}{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>57.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 57.3</annotation></semantics></math>. The radius cancels, so the angle is the same for every circle.
options: Solving <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>θ</mi><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\theta}{360} \cdot 2\pi r = r</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>180</mn><mi>π</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{180}{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>: the point is inside the circle.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y + 1</annotation></semantics></math> means <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k = -1</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>.

This is the point at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>60</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>: the coordinates are swapped.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{3}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, so this point is not even on the circle.

why.correct: Legs <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>, hypotenuse <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a\sqrt{2}</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a\sqrt{2} = 10</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>10</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{10}{\sqrt{2}}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>10</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{10\sqrt{2}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>5</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 5\sqrt{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. In a 30-60-90 triangle the sides are in the ratio <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>:</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 : \sqrt{3} : 2</annotation></semantics></math>, and the leg adjacent to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>30</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30^\circ</annotation></semantics></math> is the long leg. So the short leg, opposite <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>30</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>, is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>6</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>6</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{6}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{6\sqrt{3}}{3} = 2\sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math>. Check: the hypotenuse is then <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2\sqrt{3})^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 6^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 12</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>36</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 36</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>48</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 48</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (4\sqrt{3})^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>θ</mi><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s = \frac{\theta}{360} \cdot 2\pi r</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>θ</mi><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi = \frac{\theta}{360} \cdot 12\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>θ</mi><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\theta}{360} = \frac{1}{6}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>60</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 60^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>.

The radius is the distance from the center <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 0)</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3, -4)</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^2 = 3^2 + (-4)^2 = 25</annotation></semantics></math>. With center <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 0)</annotation></semantics></math> the equation is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + y^2 = r^2 = 25</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: The radius is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math>, and the right side is the radius squared, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3 + 4 = 7</annotation></semantics></math> adds the legs. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^2 = 3^2 + (-4)^2 = 25</annotation></semantics></math>, with center <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 0)</annotation></semantics></math>.
